newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol stake welcome on market -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Repsol stake welcome on market -analysts.

text.p: The coming privatisation of Spain's residual 10 percent state stake in petrochemical company Repsol is likely to meet solid demand, analysts say.
They expect a repeat performance of the success enjoyed by previous tranches when the shares go on sale next spring, as announced on Monday by the industry ministry.
"The previous Repsol privatisations had a very good welcome on the market. It is likely we will see good buying on the retail side," said one analyst at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.
"Institutional investors should be interested in buying as well -- this firm really is cheaper than others in Europe in the same sector," he added.
The offering is welcome even despite expectations of unflattering third-quarter results.

"Repsol has never let us down so far. This is the last time that they will offer shares directly on the market," said Juan Cueto, chief analyst at Ibersecurities. "But we'll have to look out for their results in view of some distortion factors such as competence in the sector and the volatility of petrol prices."
Repsol posted a first-half 1996 net attributable profit of 61.45 billion pesetas, down from 62.16 billion pesetas a year ago. It blamed this on its chemical division's poor performance.
But a recovery could be on the way for the second half.
A poll by Edinburgh Financial Publishing (EFP) of 22 equity analysts put 1996 net profit at 126.4 billion pesetas against 117.72 billion in 1995.

"At the fundamentals level we expect some disappointing third-quarter results, but at the same I believe they have already been discounted and will have little impact on the share," said Olga Quejido, an analyst at ODDO Securities.
Most analysts agree retail demand for the Repsol offering will be strong.

"In the previous instances we saw big interest from retail," said Ibersecurities' Cueto. Luis Moreno, an analyst at ABN Amro, agreed: "The small investors are very interested. I do expect big demand coming from there."

The shares are expected to hit the market at no less than 4,335 pesetas, which was the institutional price last time around. "It would be bad from an image point of view if it was any lower (now)," said ODDO's Quejido.
Repsol shares were up at 4,500 pesetas at 1230 GMT from Monday's close of 4,420.
In contrast with the clear support at 4,335 predicted by analysts, chartists predicted resistance around 4,500.
"If it broke through that level, we could see a potential of up to 4,700/4,800" a technical analyst said.
